Solventum Corporation is operating today as a fully independent, publicly traded company. It officially completed its spin-off from 3M on April 1, 2024, and trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker SOLV. 
3M
 +1
Manufacturing, Branding, and Corporate Status
Self-Manufacturing & Plants: Yes. Upon spinning off, Solventum assumed ownership of the manufacturing infrastructure associated with 3M's former Health Care division. According to its SEC financial disclosures, Solventum directly operates 28 manufacturing facilities (10 in the United States and 18 internationally). The company owns and runs these plants to produce its own medical consumables. 
Solventum
 +1
Branding & Product Lines: Solventum fully owns the intellectual property and rights to these legacy medical products. However, it is in the middle of a phased corporate transition. While products are manufactured by Solventum in its own plants, they are currently undergoing a multi-year rebranding process from the "3M" name to the "Solventum" brand (e.g., packaging updates transitioning 3M™ Tegaderm™ to Solventum™ Tegaderm™). 
Solventum
 +3
Film & Dressing Products Covered: Solventum’s Medical Surgical (MedSurg) segment develops and manufactures the exact items listed in your query:
Transparent Film Dressings (Tegaderm): Fully owned and produced by Solventum.
Medical Tapes and Films: Includes legacy lines like Micropore, Transpore, and Durapore.
Surgical Incise Drapes: Includes specialized antimicrobial drapes (like Ioban and Steri-Drape).
NPWT Dressing Films: Produced as part of their negative pressure wound therapy portfolio (retained from 3M's prior acquisition of Acelity/KCI).
